video.title: How a Mobile Espresso Bike Built a $3 Million Coffee Empire

summary: Vlad describes building a mobile coffee business in Vancouver, first selling drinks on regular routes and later serving private events and corporate activations. He explains how testing locations, building a returning local customer base, and using events led him to manufacture and sell coffee bikes to other operators. He says his CoffeeBike World model includes an owner community and optional add-on services, without franchise royalties or marketing fees. The interview’s main lesson is to test and execute rather than overplan, while the physical work, food regulations, and people-led sales limit how independently agents could run the operation.

acquisition.how: The route relies on choosing locations, speaking to reception staff, and building local relationships. Social posts and paid ads can be scheduled or managed with software, but much of the described acquisition is face-to-face.

onboarding.how: No customer onboarding process was described. A walk-up drink sale needs little onboarding, but a person must take and fulfil the order.

delivery.how: Preparing and serving coffee and moving or setting up the bike are physical tasks that require a person.

billing.how: No payment system or billing workflow was described. Point-of-sale payments could be handled with software, but this is an estimate rather than a transcript detail.

support.how: No customer-support system was described. A person serving the route handles in-person questions and complaints.

uk_applicability.notes: Coffee-bike routes could serve UK offices and public locations, but food-business registration, street trading permissions, and site-specific rules would need to be checked locally. The transcript describes Canadian rules, not UK ones.

risks: The first imported cart did not comply with local regulations and needed extra equipment and approval work.
The cart became overweight and difficult to move, limiting where it could operate.
A busy location with thousands of people passing through did not convert well because people were rushing between transport connections.
The business depends on physically preparing drinks and finding viable trading locations.
